text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Thousands of jobless former PLAN-fighters (People's Liberation Army of Namibia) were still camped out at the showgrounds on Thursday last night despite a plea from the complex's management that they should move on. They were promised jobs by president Sam Nujoma on Tuesday after having protested for jobs for a week.

- Controversial Mbukushu tribal head Chief Erwin Mbambo has given away more land which the Kxoe people claim is traditionally theirs, this time to a Rundu-based businessman. Sources allege that Mbambo received a lump sum of money from Wynand Peypers for the exclusive use of 20 square kilometres of land, which falls under the jurisdiction of Mbambo's rival Kxoe chief Kippie George.

- A cleric and a parliamentarian are under investigation by the Namibia Farmworkers Union (NFWU) for apparently exploiting their farmworkers. Allegations include that pensioners are being made to work for the pension money they are entitled to by law.
- The British Organisation Survival International has written an open letter to President Sam Nujoma in which it called on him to give in to the plea of the Himba people not to build a dam at Epupa.

- Terrence Stanley Shepperson, who was found guilty on charges of culpable homicide, has been sentenced to N$ 30,000 ($6,637) or four years in prison. The charges relate to the death of Shepperson's wife from a gunshot wound on their farm in the Okahandja district.
- Namibia Breweries is adamant that its biggest rival, South African Breweries, is intentionally trying to boycott Namibia's 750ml beer-packing market.
- The flow of the Kunene River has reached its lowest June level in 27 years, severely crippling the Ruacana hydropower station, which is running at a mere 14 percent of its capacity.
